request.notes: `task_type` is one of task/epic/gate and is ALWAYS sent even when it equals the upstream default, the same discipline the read side applies to `with_claims`. A `gate` requires `metadata.gate_type` in human/timer/ci/pr/external_task, and a `timer` gate additionally a parseable `metadata.ready_at`. `metadata` must NOT carry `depends_on`/`blocked_on` — dependencies are first-class edges, passed as `depends_on`, each of which creates a `blocks` edge from the predecessor; `parent_task_id` creates a `parent_child` edge parent -> new task. Both must already exist and are resolved through the SHARED id resolver: a full id, or an unambiguous prefix of at least SIX characters — shorter is `invalid_input`, several matches is `ambiguous_id_prefix` with `{id, title}` candidate RECORDS. Lens writes the project under BOTH conventions (metadata.project and the project tag, §5B.1) and carries `metadata.lens_request_id` for its own best-effort de-duplication: create mints a new id and inserts with NO uniqueness on any metadata key, so the key is a Lens-side lookup, never an upstream idempotency guarantee (T3 D10).

observed_divergences: **The success payload carries no `success` key.** Its documented return is "Dict with task_id, title, updated_at, and the resolved depends_on / parent_task_id when supplied" — the minted id IS the success signal, so `TaskCreateResult.success` is derived from it rather than read from a flag that is never sent (the first pass of this slice vendored a `success: true` that does not exist, which made every successful create normalize to success=False). `depends_on` / `parent_task_id` come back as the RESOLVED full ids and are absent when the request supplied none (`no_links`). NOT probed live, unlike the other four tools' envelopes: every create probe risks inserting a task into the operator's store, and there is no delete tool to undo it. So the three resolver envelopes here (`invalid_input` too short, `task_not_found`, `ambiguous_id_prefix` with `{id, title}` records) are transcribed from the SHARED resolver seam, probed through `lithos_task_edge_upsert` and the three task-state tools, with the field name in the message following that seam's pattern; the four validation envelopes carry the codes the source raises for rules the tool documents itself (gate_type, timer ready_at, task_type, forbidden metadata keys) with composed message text. Codes are what Lens matches on; text is never parsed.
